chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from the companions of Al-Raqiq, who said:

I bought a slave girl for Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he gave me four dinars, but I refused (to accept them). So he said to me: 'Take them!' So I took them, and he said: 'Do not take from the seller.'

key_terms.الرَّقِيقِ: Al-Raqiq (a specific companion or group of companions)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on accepting payment for facilitating a sale according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) personally compensated the narrator for facilitating the purchase of a slave girl, demonstrating the permissibility of brokerage fees (*ujrah*). The Imam’s specific instruction to accept the fee from him rather than the seller clarifies that the broker’s compensation is a right earned through service, distinct from the principal transaction price, thereby establishing a clear precedent for professional remuneration in commercial dealings within Shia jurisprudence. This incident underscores the practical application of fair compensation for intermediaries, a concept later codified in fiqh manuals regarding the rights of the *waskat* (broker).
